reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story: When building models that decide between two options, we often need a way to turn any raw score into a clear probability between zero and one. If a score grows very large or very negative, standard linear rules fail because they keep growing without bounds. We need a curve that bends gracefully, acting like a smooth valve that compresses extreme inputs into a neat range. This shaping behavior comes from the logistic function, which maps the entire real number line onto a bounded interval. By adjusting its steepness, we control how sharply the transition happens around the midpoint, making it an essential tool for smooth thresholds.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid curve maps any real input into an output strictly between $0$ and $1$. Adjust the steepness parameter to see how quickly the transition occurs around the midpoint.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve rises. Observe the output value at the fixed marker.
